criteria.text: What just-bash is and whether it runs real host executables is stated from its own source or docs

result:
result: just-bash cannot serve as HolyAgent's bash backend. It is a simulated shell with no way to run host executables, so HolyAgent's `mise`, `bun`, `git` and `holyagent` runs would all fail. Pi 1.5.0 does accept a pluggable backend, so wiring it in would be easy, but it would break the workflow.

**just-bash (sourced, fetched 2026-11-09)**
npm `just-bash` 3.6.0, Apache-2.0, updated 2026-10-01, from vercel-labs/just-bash. The README calls it beta software.
The README describes it as "A virtual bash environment with an in-memory filesystem, written in TypeScript", a TypeScript bash interpreter. The commands are in-process reimplementations: `cat`, `grep`, `sed`, `jq`, `rg`, `find`, `tar` and so on.
No `git`, `bun`, `bunx`, `mise`, `gh` or `node` appears in the command list. `curl` exists only when network is configured. Optional QuickJS, Python and sqlite run in WASM. The Security Model section says "Use Vercel Sandbox if you need a full VM with arbitrary binary execution".
Filesystems: InMemoryFs is the default. OverlayFs reads the real directory and keeps writes in memory only. ReadWriteFs writes to a real directory. The only host-process access I found is the `js-exec` QuickJS `child_process` shim (`execSync`/`spawnSync`), whose behavior I did not verify.
Cancellation is cooperative, at statement boundaries, through an `AbortSignal`. There is a `maxExecutionTimeMs` limit. Output is returned per `exec()`, not streamed. Each `exec()` resets env, cwd and functions. I found no background-process support.
Windows, macOS and Linux: the README only gives "Node >=20.19" and a browser mode. I found no platform matrix.

**Pi 1.5.0 (sourced)**
`BashOperations.exec(command, cwd, {onData, signal, timeout, env}) => Promise<{exitCode}>` is at `dist/core/tools/bash.d.ts:35-52`. `BashToolOptions.operations` (`:72`) and `createBashTool` (`:98`) take it, and `createLocalBashOperations` (`:61`) is the default. The path is `/home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-t3host/node_modules/.bun/@earendil-works+pi-coding-agent@1.5.0+8980da4117b98cd5/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`.
Existing wiring exists outside HolyAgent: `sionic-ai/pi-justbash-sandbox` (a Pi extension that replaces `bash`, `read`, `write` and `edit` with just-bash on a sandbox root), `pi-just-bash-tools` (npm) and `fuyunfei/pi-agent-just`. These are third-party and I did not read their source.
HolyAgent today uses Pi's built-in `bash`, plus `powershell` on Windows. `packages/runtime/src/pi/tools.ts:13` and `:19` list `bash` and `powershell` as tool names, and `packages/integrations/pi/src/extension.ts:1202` says Windows keeps "the default `bash` that needs Git Bash". The worktree is `/home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-t3branch`. A search of that worktree for "just-bash" found no matches. I found no repository record of the choice and did not check this session's earlier history.

**Fit (inference)**
`bunx --no-install mise run build`, `mise run verify`, `git` and the holyagent CLI through Bun all need real host binaries. just-bash has none of them, so each would fail with "command not found".
Breaks if adopted: the verify gate, commits, and every `holyagent vcs` or `assignment` command.
The one workable route is a hybrid. just-bash would handle read-only or sandboxed search and text work, while real execution stays on `createLocalBashOperations`.
Codex `apply_patch` is a separate tool and not evaluated here.

just-bash: https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash (`packages/just-bash/README.md`: virtual bash, in-memory fs, "arbitrary binary execution" only via Vercel Sandbox); https://registry.npmjs.org/just-bash/latest (3.6.0, Apache-2.0).
What just-bash is and whether it runs real host executables: it is a simulated TypeScript shell with in-process commands only, no host `git`, `bun` or `mise`; sources as above.
pi-backend: `bash.d.ts:35-52, 72, 61` in the pinned Pi host, plus HolyAgent `packages/runtime/src/pi/tools.ts:13,19` and `packages/integrations/pi/src/extension.ts:1202`.
Whether Pi 1.5.0's bash tool accepts a pluggable backend, and what HolyAgent's bash is today: Pi accepts `BashOperations` through `BashToolOptions.operations` (`bash.d.ts:35-52, 72`); HolyAgent's bash is Pi's built-in one (`tools.ts:13,19`; `extension.ts:1202`).
fit: no host executables in just-bash, so mise, bun, git and the holyagent CLI cannot run on it (inference from the README).
Whether HolyAgent's build, verify, git and CLI runs would work on it: no.
